notes.title: It's been a great week of Gunbrella!
notes.notes:
Thanks, everyone, for playing Gunbrella! 

It's incredible that today marks one week of Gunbrella being publicly available. We are proud of and humbled by the reception and the love the game has received since day one, and we are extremely happy to see everyone enjoy their experience.

A huge thanks goes out to the brave gamers who reported some of the issues that would conditionally prevent progress in some cases, which were subsequently fixed in post-launch updates. You have helped us make the game better, and for that, you are honorary doinks for life!

notes.title: Gunbrella review: a stylish 2D platformer with bullets in its brolly
notes.notes:
You can’t fault the pitch. In Gunbrella you’re a sort of cowboy dude with a shotgun that’s also an umbrella. You use the umbrella to deflect enemy projectiles, block attacks, fly up into the air like a furious Mary Poppins and zoom along ziplines. You use the shotgun, as you might reasonably expect, to do the majority of your big murdering.

Gunbrella is a classic 2D platform shooter in the style of a steampunk western. It’s like Deadwood crossed with Singin’ In The Rain, if Gene Kelly ever used his umbrella to blow holes through anyone who didn’t sufficiently praise his tap dancing. Some light exploration bits have you travelling by train from frontier towns to mining villages, much of them decorated with giant spinning cogs – so you know it’s steampunk – and populated by a small cast of quest-giving locals, pill-dispensing shopkeepers and monologuing villains.

notes.notes:
Gunbrella continues to look top-notch, the side-scrolling action-adventure serving up a does-what-it-says-on-the-tin approach to combining the floaty platforming of an umbrella with the shoot-everything-in-the-face simplicity of a gun. Now we know when we’ll be able to actually play it - and it’s soon!
